note.after_visit_summary: You saw a psychiatric nurse practitioner about feeling down for three months. You have lost interest in things you used to enjoy, trouble sleeping, low appetite with weight loss, low energy, and trouble focusing. You also had some mild anxiety. There are no vital signs that are a cause for concern today. We think you have moderate depression, which is very treatable. Your PHQ-9 score was 15 (moderate), and your GAD-7 score was 6 (mild). We are starting sertraline 25 mg once a day for one week, then increasing it to 50 mg once a day. Take it with breakfast. It may take 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. Some people get an upset stomach or headache at first, and that usually goes away. Because your aunt has bipolar disorder, call us right away if you suddenly feel wired, cannot sleep, but do not feel tired. We are setting up weekly therapy with our therapy team. You received a safety plan card. If you ever feel like hurting yourself, call or text 988 any time, or go to the nearest emergency room. Follow up with us in 4 weeks on October 19th to check how the medicine is working. If you have any questions before then, call the clinic.
